purpose: Mechanism-level baseline and ablation for CF02/CF04/CF05 without solving, clicking, or bypassing a provider challenge and without crossing ChatGPT SEND.

productionBaseline.interpretation: Browser substrate availability and provider security-boundary admissibility are empirically distinct states.

browserlessArm.route: Playwright connect_over_cdp -> Browserless /chromium -> Puppeteer launch -> Chromium

directLateAttachArm.route: direct Chromium launch -> first navigation -> Playwright connect_over_cdp

directLateAttachEnableAutomationArm.route: direct Chromium + --enable-automation -> first navigation -> late Playwright attach

directEarlyAttachNoEnableAutomationArm.route: direct Chromium without --enable-automation -> Playwright attach -> navigation

cf04Cf05Ablation.finding: For navigator.webdriver specifically, --enable-automation is sufficient to reproduce the observed Browserless value, while early-vs-late CDP attachment did not change the value in the direct-Chromium arms.

stableAcrossBothArms.userAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/153.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

cf02TransportExperiment.finding: JA3 changed on every fresh connection in both arms; a one-shot JA3 difference is therefore not path-attribution evidence here. JA4, PeetPrint and HTTP/2 fingerprint were stable and identical across both arms.

currentModelUpdate.CF02: No stable Browserless-vs-direct difference observed in JA4, PeetPrint or HTTP/2 fingerprint under same Chromium/network. JA3 is noisy and must not be treated as a one-shot discriminator.
currentModelUpdate.CF04: navigator.webdriver difference is real and reproducible; launch presentation via --enable-automation is a sufficient mechanism for this observable.
currentModelUpdate.CF05: Attachment timing alone did not affect navigator.webdriver, but other control-protocol/execution-context side channels remain unmeasured and open.
currentModelUpdate.CF08: Production challenge remains observed; no experiment here establishes that CF04 or CF05 caused that challenge.

explicitNonClaims: The experiment does not identify the provider-authoritative cause of the ChatGPT Cloudflare challenge.
The experiment does not show that changing --enable-automation would make ChatGPT admissible.
The experiment does not test or automate challenge solving.
The experiment does not cross ChatGPT SEND.
The experiment does not establish that Browserless-specific CDP listeners are irrelevant; those side channels remain unmeasured.
